name: Followers of Set of Note (Wolves at the Door Lore)

text.content: Once caliph of Cairo and a natural target for Setite manipulation given his position, al-Hakim instead fell under the sway of the Malkavians and now serves as their ghoul, mad among the mad. The Followers of Set initially welcomed the prospect — reasoning that a madman would be all the easier to steer — but every overture toward him instead produced wild, unpredictable results, culminating in vicious persecutions against the Setites and the wider Egyptian population alike. Setite elders now consider al-Hakim more trouble than he is worth and privately favor his destruction, though few among the clan can resist the temptation to test their wits against him and his Malkavian keepers. Storytellers can use al-Hakim as an unpredictable wildcard in Cairo politics: a nominal figure of great mortal authority whose true masters and motives are impossible for outsiders to read.

A leader among the Decadent faction of the Followers of Set, Khay'tall has built his following in part by recruiting from outside the clan's traditional Egyptian bloodlines — a practice that scandalizes the Hierophants, who see it as reckless dilution of Set's blood, and a point of pride for the Decadents, who consider it evidence of their god's growing reach into Europe. Khay'tall is noted for inducting other Cainites (not merely mortals) into service of Set through a rite resembling the Setites' own religious Embrace; such converts lack Set's actual blood and are regarded by true Setites as little better than especially favored ghouls, even as rival clans who discover them typically assume they are full Setites or their thralls. Hierophants attribute Khay'tall's greater success at this practice to simple lack of selectivity rather than any special gift, but his faction's numbers continue to grow regardless.
